evidence.content: Harborline reported $18.4M revenue and $3.1M adjusted EBITDA for FY2026 (audited).
Revenue CAGR was 11% over FY2023–FY2026, driven by two anchor contracts.
The two anchor contracts represent 58% of revenue and renew in 14 months.
Management projects 18% revenue growth for FY2027 on new lane expansion.
Fleet average age is 9.2 years vs. industry median 6.5; capex backlog estimated at $4–6M.
Founder-CEO intends to retire within 12 months; no named successor in place.
Comparable regional freight acquisitions closed at 5.5x–7.0x EBITDA in the last 18 months.
Whether the anchor contracts renew at current rates is disputed by diligence.

risks.description: 58% of revenue tied to two contracts renewing in 14 months; loss of one impairs debt service.
risks.name: Anchor contract non-renewal

risks.description: $4–6M fleet capex not reflected in projections; erodes free cash flow in years 1–2.
risks.name: Capex backlog underfunded

risks.description: Founder-CEO retirement with no successor; operational continuity risk post-close.
risks.name: Leadership vacuum

assumptions: anchor contracts renew at current rates
lane expansion delivers half of projected growth
scenarios.name: Base case: contracts renew, lanes expand
scenarios.projected_outcome: EBITDA $3.8M by FY2028; 6.2x entry multiple de-levers to 4.1x

assumptions: replacement lanes take 18 months to ramp
scenarios.name: Downside: one anchor lost
scenarios.projected_outcome: EBITDA $1.6M FY2027; covenant breach risk on acquisition debt

terms: $42M enterprise value, 60% cash / 40% rollover equity, close targeted Q1
